description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court clearly erred in refusing to sentence Mr. McGann to a recidivist life sentence, as neither disproportionate sentencing nor substantive due process arguments validated the lower court's decision.

name: ARMSTEAD, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court did not err in accepting the petitioner's stipulation without counsel as he knowingly and intelligently waived his right, and the termination of parental rights was warranted due to his repeated failures to correct conditions of abuse and neglect.

name: BUNN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the case should have been set for oral argument and that the petitioner's equal protection rights argument, stemming from the disparate treatment of heroin and oxycodone cases, deserves a full and considered opinion.

name: WALKER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that while the circuit court erred in not crediting the full time served, the error was harmless because the petitioner ultimately received credit for all time served in a separate county's sentencing.

name: WOOTON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Special Acts requiring Cabell County to include library and park funding on its excess levy proposals violate equal protection guarantees because they create a discriminatory classification among counties without a compelling state interest.

name: Justice William R. Wooton
description: Concurred, argued that the 2018 amendment to the burglary statute has a constitutional defect because its title failed to properly notify legislators and the public of the removal of the 'of another' requirement, but found the defect harmless in this case as the jury was correctly instructed on that element.

name: HUTCHISON JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the 2020 recidivist statute did not violate ex post facto principles as it did not increase punishment or lengthen the sentence compared to the 2000 statute, and the life sentence was constitutionally proportionate because all three felony offenses involved actual or threatened violence.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Hope Scholarship Act is constitutional as the West Virginia Constitution's "free schools" clause does not prohibit the Legislature from enacting additional educational initiatives, and the Act does not impinge on a child's fundamental right to education or improperly direct public funds.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Dissented, argued that the Hope Scholarship Act is unconstitutional because it violates the West Virginia Constitution's mandate for a system of free public schools, denies public education its preferred status, and fails strict scrutiny review by reducing public school funding.

name: HUTCHISON CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court completely lacked jurisdiction to review as-applied challenges to WVSSAC rules and clearly erred in finding the Residence-Transfer Rule facially unconstitutional, as it meets the rational basis test by promoting academics over athletics and does not violate equal protection.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Recused himself from the decision.

name: JUDGE COURRIER

name: HUTCHISON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the mid-deliberation juror substitution violated Rule 24(c) and the trial court failed to take extraordinary precautions to overcome the presumption of prejudice, thus requiring reversal and a new trial.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the defendant was not prejudiced by the juror substitution and received a fair trial, so the convictions should be affirmed.

name: Wooton, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court's failure to re-administer the juror oath to the recalled alternate juror was a fundamental, structural error that rendered the conviction invalid.

name: ARMSTEAD, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that claims for excessive force by police officers under the West Virginia Constitution must be analyzed under the specific search and seizure clause (Article III, Section 6) and not the general due process clause (Article III, Section 10), and that claims under Section 10 are redundant as no private right of action for monetary damages exists under Section 6.

name: JUSTICE ALAN D. MOATS
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: Armstead, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Judge Goldston's actions constituted an unlawful search and an exercise of executive power, violating the Code of Judicial Conduct and warranting censure and a $1,000 fine.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Dissented, argued that while discipline was warranted, the conduct was more a legal error than an ethical violation, and an admonishment with a $1,000 fine would be more appropriate, deferring to the Judicial Hearing Board's recommendation.

name: JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Disqualified himself from the decision.

name: HUTCHISON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that prior decisions (Hall and Divita) were incorrectly decided by automatically reversing revocation orders for an officer's failure to provide a blood test, and that a new test should evaluate the violation in the context of the entire record.

name: WOOTON, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's new point of law is a dangerous exercise in futility, improperly creates judicial restraints on a legislatively prescribed due process right, and may invite misapplication in future criminal DUI proceedings, especially given the imminent termination of the administrative revocation procedure.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE JENKINS
description: Dissented, arguing that defendants are entitled to a jury trial for public nuisance claims and that the 2015 Act should apply, allowing for non-party fault.

name: ARMSTEAD, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that while a jury trial is necessary for intertwined claims, the majority erred by denying defendants' statutory right to allocate fault under the 2015 Act, which should apply to the claims.

name: JUSTICE HUTCHISON
description: Concurred, arguing that the majority opinion skillfully addresses defendants' concerns, upholds jury trial rights, and allows the Mass Litigation Panel flexibility to manage the complex opioid litigation.

name: JUSTICE WOOTON
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing that the Panel's decision for a bench trial on public nuisance claims was not clearly erroneous, but dissented from the majority's analysis for interfering with the Mass Litigation Panel's authority.

name: WALKER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that an Emergency Protective Order (EPO) is not a de facto search warrant and cannot authorize law enforcement to enter and search a home for firearms without meeting probable cause standards required by the Fourth Amendment.

name: ARMSTEAD, J.
description: Concurred that an EPO is not equivalent to a search warrant and with remanding the case, but dissented from reversing the conviction, arguing for further development on whether there was implied consent for officers to enter the home.
